## Natural history notes

A medium-sized songbird characterized by its gray upperparts, pale underparts, long tail, slender slightly curved bill, and bold white wing patches that flash in flight. In Florida, it is common in yards, parks, roadsides, scrub, pine flatwoods, forest edges, agricultural areas, and other open or semi-open habitats with shrubs and scattered trees. It feeds on insects, spiders, berries, and small fruits, often foraging on the ground or in low vegetation, and is well known for its loud, varied song and ability to mimic other birds and sounds.
